headline.label: Jim's literal 20 day rule (sign of the 20 day average move, long/short, hold 1 day), out-of-sample net Sharpe
headline.value: Crypto perps 0.72 (2024-01 -> 2026-10) | Commodities -0.18, FX 0.08 (2013 -> 2024-09) | All-markets equal-risk portfolio 0.63 (2018 -> 2026-10)

stats.version: all_markets equal-risk portfolio, N=20, sign_ls (Jim's literal rule), each market vol-targeted to 10%/yr, net of costs
stats.avg_unit: bp per trade, net, 1x notional, averaged over all markets
stats.costs: crypto: Binance taker 0.05% + 0.02% slippage = 7 bp per side per unit of position change (a flip = 2 sides); futures/FX: 1 bp per side (Moon Dev assumption, video gives none); TSLA/SPY: 1 bp + half a cent per share per side. Zero-cost numbers shown next to every net number. No funding charged on perps (not in the task).

after_fees.version: all_markets N=20 long_only, net of trading costs, OOS 2018-01-01 on, scaled to 10% vol with IS vol (x2.66)

claims.claim: The 20 day average move predicts the next day (trend following works)
claims.test: sign(mean of last 20 daily returns), long/short, hold 1 day; pooled t-stat per asset class + all-markets portfolio Sharpe
claims.result: Pooled t-stat of next-day P&L of the 20 day sign rule (zero cost): crypto perps 4.39, commodities 0.15, FX 0.56, index futures 0.82. All-markets portfolio Sharpe 0.45 zero cost, 0.36 net.
claims.verdict: VERIFIED in crypto (t = 4.4), BUSTED in commodities and FX since 2000 (t = 0.15 and 0.56)

claims.claim: Try 10 day, 15 day... 'see what worked best': some N beats 20 out of sample
claims.test: pick N in 2..250 on in-sample net Sharpe only, report out-of-sample
claims.result: crypto_perps: IS-picked N=193 OOS 0.24 vs N=20 OOS 0.72; commodities: IS-picked N=104 OOS 0.20 vs N=20 OOS -0.18; fx: IS-picked N=128 OOS 0.46 vs N=20 OOS 0.08; index_futures: IS-picked N=155 OOS 0.67 vs N=20 OOS 0.26; all_markets: IS-picked N=125 OOS 0.46 vs N=20 OOS 0.63
claims.verdict: NOT PROVEN: the in-sample best N won in 3 of 5 groups but lost in crypto (0.24 vs 0.72) and in the all-markets portfolio (0.46 vs 0.63). Picking N in-sample overstated Sharpe by 0.42 (all markets) to 1.52 (crypto perps).

claims.claim: Trend following faded 'because everyone could see that'
claims.test: calendar-year Sharpe of the 20 day rule (zero cost), straight-line fit vs year
claims.result: crypto_spot_long: -0.128 Sharpe/yr (p=0.33, 2018-2026); crypto_perps: -0.166 Sharpe/yr (p=0.27, 2020-2026); commodities: -0.025 Sharpe/yr (p=0.36, 2001-2024); fx: -0.031 Sharpe/yr (p=0.15, 2000-2024); index_futures: +0.012 Sharpe/yr (p=0.62, 2001-2024); stocks_SPY: -0.005 Sharpe/yr (p=0.89, 2010-2026)
claims.verdict: NOT PROVEN: the yearly Sharpe trend line slopes down in crypto (-0.17 a year), commodities and FX, but no slope is significant (all p > 0.15). Commodities and FX were already near zero for 2000-2024, which fits Jim's story that it died by the 80s.

claims.claim: It works 'not beautifully': near 50% wins, long losing stretches
claims.result: Trade win rate 32.6% over 9649 trades, day win rate 51.3%, longest drawdown 3237 days, max DD -11.8%
claims.verdict: VERIFIED: 51% winning days, 33% winning trades, one drawdown lasted 3,237 days (May 2011 -> Mar 2020)

price_replay.symbol: BTCUSDT-perp (Binance), daily, signal = sign of 20 day mean return (+1 long, -1 short)

takeaways: Jim's 20 day rule still works in crypto: 0.72 net Sharpe out of sample on 16 Binance perps (2024-01 -> 2026-10), beating buy and hold of the same coins at equal risk (0.47).

In commodities and FX (Jim's own markets) it is dead from 2000 on: 20 day OOS net Sharpe -0.18 for oil, gold, silver, gas and 0.08 for four FX pairs. That fits his 'by the 80s it wasn't' line. We have no 1960s-80s data to see the good years.

'See what worked best' is a trap: the best in-sample N for crypto was 193 days (Sharpe 1.76), which fell to 0.24 out of sample. Plain 20 kept 0.72. Per coin, the best IS N averaged 1.98 Sharpe in sample and -0.09 out of sample.
Slower trends (N about 100 to 190) were the in-sample winners in commodities, FX and index futures, and held up out of sample better than 20 there.
It fades, but slowly and noisily: crypto's yearly Sharpe falls about 0.17 a year (2020: 2.15, 2026: 1.12) but the slope is not significant (p = 0.27).
Not beautiful, just like Jim said: 51% winning days, 33% winning trades, and one drawdown in the all-markets portfolio lasted almost 9 years (2011 -> 2020).
Shorter bars die on costs: the same rule on 1h crypto bars has positive gross Sharpe (1.50 OOS at N=20 bars) but every N goes negative after 7 bp a side.
Jim's fees eat most of it: the best honest OOS version (all markets, N=20, long-only, 10% vol) made 11.2% a year before fees, 7.4% after 2 and 20, 3.5% after 5 and 44.
